newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Israel accepts Jewish settlement "pause".
newsitem.headline: PLO says Israel accepts Jewish settlement "pause".

text.p: PLO officials said on Sunday Israel had agreed in principle to an unspecified "pause" in Jewish settlement building, clearing the way for a meeting with Israeli negotiators in Cairo.

"The change in the Israeli government's position on this issue in particular and its acceptance in principle to a 'pause' in settlement activities made it possible to hold this meeting at the experts level," Marwan Kanafani, spokesman to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, told Reuters from Cairo.
The meeting was due to begin at 1400 GMT in Cairo.

But Israeli officials insisted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government remained committed to building settlements on land occupied in 1967 in the West Bank, including in Arab East Jerusalem, as well as in the Gaza Strip.
Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, part of the Israeli delegation to the Cairo talks, told Israel Radio: "Nothing was promised in order to ensure a meeting today."

"There's no chance Israel agreed to stop the construction on Har Homa or in the settlements," he said. Talks have been stuck since Israel broke ground three months ago for Har Homa Jewish settlement on an East Jerusalem hill Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.
